consensus_summary: Works are a person's deeds or actions understood as the outward expression and evidence of inner spiritual state: good works are the fruit and evidence of genuine faith and grace, evil works the fruit of a sinful or unregenerate heart, and works serve as the evidentiary basis at final judgment. Alternatives include the New Perspective's 'works of the law' as covenant boundary markers, Catholic/Orthodox cooperative merit, and works as self-effort opposed to grace.
book_summary: A work is simply a deed and is not a synonym for obedience. A deed becomes obedience only when it fulfills a legitimate command and disobedience when it conflicts with a command; context, not the word itself, separately identifies whether 'works' concerns wages, duty, or faith made visible. The book flags the common teaching (works as human effort opposed to faith, with good works as post-salvation evidence) as the view it is adjusting.
consensus_core_identification: Works = human deeds that intrinsically carry moral/spiritual freight, functioning as the visible fruit and evidence of inner faith (good works) or sin (evil works), and as the record judged by God.
book_core_identification: Works = deeds per se, morally neutral in themselves; their status as obedience or disobedience is determined externally by relation to a command, and their soteriological role (wages, duty, faith made visible) is determined by context rather than being inherent to the word.
boundary_disagreement: The consensus treats works as inherently evidential of inner state (good works flow from faith, evil works from the flesh). The book denies that 'works' itself encodes obedience or evidence; the same deed-vocabulary covers neutral deeds, commanded duty (Luke 17:7-10), wage-earning labor (Rom 4:4-5), and faith made visible (Jas 2:21-22), with obedience/disobedience assigned only by reference to a command (Ex 18:20; Mic 6:16). This reclassifies the consensus's blanket 'good = fruit of faith / evil = fruit of flesh' scheme into a command-relative and context-dependent taxonomy, while retaining deeds as the referent and retaining 'faith made visible' as one legitimate contextual sense.
rationale: Both sides identify works as deeds, so the central referent survives; this is not DIVERGENT. But the book materially changes the conditions: it rejects treating 'works' as a unitary symbol of obedience/effort or of inner spiritual state, insisting the word is neutral and that moral valence attaches only via command and context. This narrows the consensus's evidential-fruit reading to just one contextual case among several (duty, wages, obedience) and rejects the common-view framing (works as human effort versus faith with good works as automatic evidence) that Responses A, B, and D make central. That is a real boundary and classification disagreement within the same category, making REFINED the correct verdict rather than MATCH. It is not NOVEL because 'deeds' is exactly the consensus category, and Response C's contextual-plurality note partially anticipates the book's context-sensitivity.
strongest_objection: One could argue MATCH: the consensus already recognizes that 'works' means deeds whose significance varies by context (Response C explicitly denies a single settled symbolic meaning and lists duty, judgment-record, law, and evidential senses), so the book's command-relative taxonomy may be a mere reorganization of what the consensus already contains, with the 'not a synonym for obedience' claim being a distinction the consensus never actually asserted in the first place.
